newsitem.title: LIBYA: Gaddafi says meeting a defeat for U.S., Britain.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi says meeting a defeat for U.S., Britain.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi said a meeting of African ministers in Tripoli was a defeat for the United States and Britain who were intent on isolating the North African country.

"Who is isolated now? America was telling the world that Libya was isolated. It is America which is isolated, and Britain too," a jubilant Gaddafi told some 40 ministers from Africa at a banquet in the Azizia battacks in Tripoli.

Ministers and officials from 52 African countries travelled this week to Libya by road for an Organisation of African Unity council meeting in Tripoli because of an air embargo imposed since 1992 by the United Nations over the Lockerbie bombing.
Dressed in an African-style clear blue djellaba, Gaddafi was in an upbeat mood and talked to the assembly for more than 2-1/2 hours, ending his speech in the early hours of Thursday.
"This is a great day. This is a defiance summit...Today we have challenged and defeated America, and we will defeat it on the ground if it comes here," he said.
The OAU said the meeting in Tripoli was a show of solidarity with the people of Libya.

"Our meeting here, in Tripoli, is of particular significance. It is an expression of our solidarity with the people of Libya at a time when they're confronted with adversity as a result of the imposition of sanctions," OAU Secretary General Salim Ahmed Salim said at the opening session of the three-day council on Wednesday.
"The very impressive presence of foreign ministers and other Ministers in Tripoli speaks eloquently of that solidarity," he added.

The U.N. sanctions, including an embargo on flights to and from Libya, were imposed for Tripoli's failure to hand over two Libyan suspects for trial in the United States or Britain for the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am flight over Lockerbie, Scotland, that killed 270 people.
The security council also asked Tripoli to cooperate with France in the investigation over the mid-air blast of a French airliner over Niger in 1989.
Gaddafi said Libya has fulfilled this last request when it received a French magistrate last year who interrogated several people in Libya.

"The problem between Libya and France was resolved. The magistrate came and made a positive report. It is not important thereafter that the sentence at the trial will be a condemnation or not," he added.

Gaddafi also said Libya had cooperated fully with Britain over its ties with the Irish Republican Army, whose guerrillas are fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland. But Britain had refused to improve relations with Tripoli.
"Britain says it was for solidarity with America," he added.
